Hi Jason — thanks for the list. Below are concrete answers you can share with your security/compliance team. High-level first, then specifics.

High-level:
- Hosted API (default): 
  • By default, Redwood collects request and response data for up to 30 days to support debugging, abuse detection, and model quality monitoring.
  • We provide a per-account option to disable request/response logging ("no-store") during the API key creation or via the Console; this prevents prompts and outputs from being written to our request logs.
  • For customers on Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments, request/response content is not collected by our hosted control plane; logs remain within customer-managed infrastructure unless you opt into sharing.

Detailed breakdown:
- Prompts & Outputs: 
  • Hosted (default): Stored in encrypted logs for up to 30 days; can be disabled (no-store) to prevent storage of plaintext prompts/outputs.
  • Dedicated/Private: We do not persist customer prompts/outputs in Redwood-managed logs; any logging is controlled by the customer's environment and policy.

- PII in outputs: 
  • If logging is enabled, outputs that contain PII are treated the same as any output and are stored in encrypted logs for the retention window. If you enable no-store, these are not written to logs.

- Metadata & telemetry: 
  • We retain request metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts, response latency, and redacted IP hash) for 90 days for billing and operational analytics.
  • We do not persist KV caches or internal ephemeral caches beyond the inference lifecycle; they are not stored to disk for hosted requests.

- Data residency: 
  • Hosted customers can choose region-specific endpoints (us, eu, apac). Selecting an EU region routes request processing and persistent logs to EU-hosted infrastructure.
  • For stronger guarantees (data residency + no-hosted-logs), we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private.

- Retention & deletion: 
  • Hosted default retention: 30 days for request/response content; 90 days for metadata.
  • Shorter retention windows are available by contract for Enterprise deals.
  • We support on-demand deletion of stored request/response data for the account; we can coordinate deletion once you sign the pilot agreement.

- Access & audit: 
  • All access to logs is audited. We can provide access logs and an export for audits under NDA.

Next steps we can take for Acme's pilot:
1) Spin up an EU-hosted API key and enable the no-store flag for the pilot environment.
2) Provide a DPA and SOC 2 artifacts under an NDA (link in related links).
3) If required, scope Redwood Dedicated/private pilot for full residency and zero-hosted-log guarantees — I can loop in Solutions Engineering for sizing.

Attachment: redwood-pii-data-retention-2028.pdf
Link: https://redwood.app/compliance/soc2 (SOC 2 access under NDA)

Let me know if you want a 30-minute follow-up to go over the technical controls.
